new_statements.quote: Neither in the phonological section nor anywhere else in the grammar is there any discussion of suprasegmental features such as tone, whether it is phonemically functional or not, nor of word or sentence stress. This is surprising in view of the author's obviously extensive knowledge of the language and familiarity with linguistic description. The only mention of word stress is contained in one sentence in a larger footnote as a possible explanation of a lengthened vowel in one verb (''It could be explained by stress assignment to the penultimate syllable, a process which could have caused the lengthened vowels in the class 4 verbs'' (p. 39).

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record. Not a placement statement: it establishes that the primary grammar (Barclay 2006/2008) is silent on stress and tone apart from one speculative footnote pointing to penultimate stress; a firm statement for west2594 would have to come from Purba, Warwer & Futubun 1993 Fonologi Bahasa Dani Barat (HathiTrust search-only) or fieldwork.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The reviewer reports that Barclay's 2008 grammar (the published Monash thesis, the fullest description of Western Dani) gives NO account of word stress, sentence stress or tone; the only mention of stress anywhere in the grammar is a footnote (Barclay p. 39) that tentatively invokes 'stress assignment to the penultimate syllable' as a possible cause of vowel lengthening in class 4 verbs. So: no stated stress rule; a speculative penultimate-stress hint only.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the penult remark is offered by Barclay only as a hypothesis for lengthened vowels in class 4 verbs
new_statements.identity_note: Western Dani (Lani), west2594, as described in Barclay 2008 A Grammar of Western Dani (Lincom; published version of the 2006 Monash PhD thesis); the review does not name a particular dialect area.

tone_statements.citation: Purba, Theodorus T., Onesimus Warwer & Reimundus Futubun. 1993. Fonologi Bahasa Dani Barat. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xv+112 pp.
tone_statements.quote: 2.5 Unsur Suprasegmental Sejauh data yang dikumpulkan belum ditemui adanya tekanan , nada , dan panjang pendeknya bunyi yang dapat mengubah arti suatu kata. Dengan demikian, dapat dikatakan bahwa tebnan, panjangnya suara, dan nada bukan fonemik dalam BDB. … Tekanan pada BDB tidak tetap. Jadi, tekanan tidak seperti dalam bahasa Indonesia yang pada umumnya diletakkan pada suku kedua dari belakang. … 5. Tekanan. nada. dan jeda tidak fonemik .
tone_statements.translation: 2.5 Suprasegmental elements. As far as the data collected go, no stress, tone or length of sounds has been found that can change the meaning of a word. Thus it can be said that stress, length and tone are not phonemic in Western Dani (BDB). ... Stress in BDB is not fixed. So stress is not as in Indonesian, where it is generally placed on the penultimate syllable. ... [Conclusions] 5. Stress, tone and juncture are not phonemic.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.5 Unsur Suprasegmental, pp. 36-37; conclusion item 5, sec. 5.1 Kesimpulan, p. 78
tone_statements.summary: Tone, stress and length stated non-phonemic: no pitch difference changes word meaning in the data. Stress not fixed, often final in trisyllables. Only a family-level remark that TNG often has tone.

sources.note: Verb tense/temporality only; no phonology or stress. Notes (p. 15) that Purba dkk. studied the phonology in 1993 and morphology in 1994; bibliography (p. 22) gives Purba dkk. 1994 Morfologi Bahasa Dani Barat and Purba dkk. 2000 'Variasi struktur bahasa daerah di Irian Jaya', Jurnal MLI 18(1): 77-98.

sources.citation: Bromley, H. Myron. 1961. The Phonology of Lower Grand Valley Dani: A Comparative Structural Study of Skewed Phonemic Patterns (Verhandelingen KITLV 34). 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff. doi:10.26530/oapen_613378
sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'The pattern of Western Dani' (pp. 8-10, data from Gordon Larson for Ilaga/Tinak, Sheila Draper and Bromley for North Baliem, Ross Bartel for Hablifoeri) gives only the consonant/vowel pattern and distribution of WD; it says nothing about WD stress. The stress statement in sec. 3.132 (p. 49: 'The phonological word consists of a syllable or group of syllables with only one primary word stress. Since this stress occurs on final syllables of words in most cases..') describes Lower Grand Valley Dani (a different language), not west2594.
